correctness.rationale: Spanning connected tight graph implies integer vertices and, on the bipartite three-edge parallel paths, saturation on every edge. The terminal difference is ±1 or ±3; the ±1 cases are three states X,Y,Z per path. For counts a,b,c, the squared Euclidean normal norm is (m+1)/2+2(a+c)-2(c-a)^2/(m+1); the ±3 normal has squared norm (m+9)/2. Strict comparison proves all max norms come from balanced X/Z words when m≥3. The centrally symmetric convex body has a largest ball centered at 0. Exact contact-normal linear algebra proves ranks m (even m) and m+1 (odd m); strict slack of noncontacts proves the affine center dimensions. Standalone exact check verified 708 full raw facets for m=3,4,5 and 19668 signed path words for m=3..8. Finite checks are corroborative, not infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The complete canonical Euclidean facet-distance multiset, radius, tangent multiplicities, and center-locus affine-dimension parity are separate from the earlier, explicitly acknowledged theta total-facet enumeration. Same-object sources were compared by implications, not matching title or parameters; none of the inspected results directly states or algebraically reduces to these Euclidean-shell and rank claims without new norm optimization.
residual_risks: An explicit result framed as maximum centered variance of graph-metric 1-Lipschitz functions for equal three-edge theta paths could imply the inradius and perhaps the contact ranks; this has not been globally ruled out.
Facet labeling is known. The result should be credited only for the Euclidean norm optimization and incenter geometry, not for an already-known total facet count.
No theorem for arbitrary unequal path lengths or alternative Euclidean embeddings is established.

value.rationale: Generalized theta graphs are a standard natural family of overlapping cycles, with arbitrary number of identical length-three paths. The exact canonical Euclidean facet-distance multiset and its extremal shells give an invariant not recovered from the known total facet count. The central-binomial contact count and parity change in the affine dimension of all max-ball centers are structural all-dimensional phenomena, not small or arbitrary numerical improvements. The proof explicitly motivates and resolves the complete exact invariant within the specified family.
